answer: Each identity must post one opal bond: a scarce, non-transferable capital lock that cannot be bought wholesale, split, or run in parallel — one bond per head, priced at the full rate no matter how many heads an operator runs. When one head cheats, the whisper of that fraud triggers forfeiture of the whole bond, and the loss sends a ripple through every other bond the operator holds, because bonds are linked by a shared operator fingerprint. Splitting into n clones therefore costs n full bonds while honest influence stays intact, so each extra head makes attack strictly more expensive.
